title: Add phase-aware regression scorer and staged fallback policy for canary guard
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation:
We continue to see noisy, traffic-dependent latency regressions during rollouts where short microbursts or phase shifts (e.g., nightly batch windows) cause spurious canary failures. Existing canary detectors are effective at threshold-based anomalies but lack a compact score that summarizes cross-signal regression severity and confidence while being resilient to traffic modality changes.

What this PR introduces:
1) Regression Scorer: a compact, phase-aware scoring component that fuses latency percentiles, tail-quantile drift, and throughput deltas into a single normalized regression score. The scorer uses per-route phase segmentation (learned from time-of-day and concurrency histograms) to normalize expected behavior, applies microburst normalization (short-window smoothing with an adaptive bandwidth), and computes a traffic-weighted confidence that downweights low-sample, high-variance observations. Score output: {score, confidence, contributing_signals}.

2) Staged Fallback Policy: a rollout guard that consumes the regression score and implements a three-stage response: soft-throttle (reduce canary traffic by X%), partial-fallback (route high-cost/low-priority traffic to cheaper compatible model variants), and full-failover (immediate rollback to previous model version in extreme regressions). The policy is parameterized by score thresholds, minimum confidence, and cooldown windows.

3) Integration points: canary evaluator (services/canary/evaluator.py) now emits scorer metrics and tags; rollout controller (services/rollout/controller.go) implements staged fallback hooks; console dashboard and alerts (monitoring/dashboards/latency-regression-scorer.jsonnet) visualize score + signal breakdown.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Phase-aware normalization reduces false positives caused by predictable diurnal/concurrency patterns but requires an initial warmup period per route (two weeks recommended).
- Microburst normalization prevents single-minute spikes from triggering aggressive actions but slightly increases detection latency for sustained degradations; tuned default favors faster detection for high-SLA routes.
- Confidence aggregation avoids acting on low-volume noise; operators can override the minimum confidence for critical routes.

Implementation highlights (single-string summary):
- New scorer implementation (services/canary/scorer.py) with vectorized percentile fusion and bootstrap-based confidence estimator.
- Fast C-backed aggregator for per-second histograms (pkg/telemetry/histogram_accel.c + bindings) reused by the scorer to keep CPU overhead low.
- Rollout controller hooks and a new staged fallback policy implementation (services/rollout/fallback_policy.go).
- End-to-end smoke harness and regression tests added under tests/perf/test_regression_scorer.py and e2e/perf/canary_staged_fallback.sh.

Commits summary:
- feat(canary): add phase segmentation model and scorer core
- perf(telemetry): add histogram accel bindings and binding tests
- feat(rollout): staged fallback policy and controller hooks
- docs: runbook and console dashboard for scorer-driven rollouts
- test: add unit and integration tests, CI perf harness

Files changed (high level):
- services/canary/scorer.py
- services/canary/evaluator.py (emit scorer metrics)
- services/rollout/fallback_policy.go
- pkg/telemetry/histogram_accel.c
- monitoring/dashboards/latency-regression-scorer.jsonnet
- docs/runbooks/perf-regression-scorer.md
- tests/perf/test_regression_scorer.py
- e2e/perf/canary_staged_fallback.sh

Testing and CI notes:
- Unit tests cover scorer numeric stability and confidence calibration.
- Perf suite includes synthetic microburst injection against the scorer and validates staged fallback paths in a canary harness.
- CPU overhead measured at ~0.8% for scorer on production canary traffic in benchmark lab.

Runbook / operator guidance (short):
- Default configuration enables soft-throttle on score > 0.6 and confidence > 0.75; partial-fallback at score > 0.75; full-failover at score > 0.9 with sustained window 3m.
- To enable for a route: set route.canary.scorer.enabled=true and choose a fallback profile (low-latency / cost-optimized).

Linked work: ENG-2143 (canary scoring baseline), ENG-3321 (staged fallback policy RFC).
